newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Gazprom seeks bonds to pay for gas to Moldova.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom seeks bonds to pay for gas to Moldova.

text.p: Russian natural gas monopoly Gazprom has asked Moldova to hand over Treasury bonds worth $140 million as part of a deal to restructure Moldovan debts for gas imports, a Finance Ministry official told Reuters.
But Moldova hoped to buy the bonds back at a 15 percent discount soon and would borrow on international financial markets to find the cash to redeem the securities, he added.
"Gazprom insists we give the bonds by April 1. After we do that, we will seek to buy the debt back at a discount," said Victor Cibotari, deputy director of the ministry's treasury department.

The transactions are part of a deal signed between Gazprom and the Moldovan government in July 1996 under which the government took responsibility for part of Moldova's debts to Gazprom and pledged to issue bonds to cover the debt.
The former Soviet republic is issuing 2,000 securities worth a nominal $70,000 each, to be repaid in seven years at 7.5 percent annual interest rate with a two-year grace period.
Under the deal Gazprom pledged to freeze penalties for the arrears and allow Moldova to just pay for current supplies.
Moldovan Prime Minister Ion Ciubuc told reporters Moldova's debts to Gazprom were $500 million on March 1, or $100 million more than at the time when the deal was signed.

The Chisinau government has accepted responsibility for $140 million of Moldova's debts. Companies and other agents must pay the rest themselves. The breakaway Dnestr region owes $260 million of the total.
Cibotari said Gazprom had appointed Moscow-based Natsionalny Reservny Bank as its depository for the bonds and the Moldovan government was expected to name the bank as its payment agent.
He said a Moldovan delegation would go to Moscow later this week to work out final details of the deal.

"After that we will consider proposals to issue bonds through German Dresdner Bank, Austrian Creditanstalt Investment Bank or Japanease Daiwa European to get the money to redeem the Gazprom debt," Cibotari said.
Moldova plans to place its first $70 million issue of Eurobonds on international markets in April and made a $30 million international private placement last year.
Moldova consumes some three billion cubic meters of gas a year and currently pays Gazprom $58 per 1,000 cubic metres.
